trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Amsterdam Airport Schiphol at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take the direct train from Schiphol to Amsterdam Centraal (€5, ~17 mins), then make your way to Canal House Amsterdam to check in and drop off luggage.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a self-guided walk along the Herengracht and Prinsengracht canals near the hotel. Explore the Jordaan neighborhood — one of Amsterdam's most charming districts with free street art, independent boutiques, and picturesque bridges. Visit the Westerkerk church (free exterior, small fee inside) for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Leidseplein square to soak up the local atmosphere. Grab dinner at a nearby budget-friendly spot and enjoy your first evening in Amsterdam at a relaxed pace.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at Schiphol Airport before or after landing — budget around €5-8.
meals.lunch: Pick up a broodje (Dutch sandwich) or stroopwafel from a street stall or Albert Heijn supermarket near Centraal Station for €3-6.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dampkring Café or Foodhallen street food market in the Jordaan area — budget €10-15 for hearty Dutch or international street food.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the 13:00 arrival. Purchase an OV-chipkaart (public transport card) at Schiphol for €7.50 deposit — it will save money on all future tram and bus rides. Consider buying a 72-hour GVB transit pass (€21) if you plan to use trams frequently.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Rijksmuseum when it opens at 9:00 to beat the crowds. Spend 2-3 hours exploring the Netherlands' premier art and history museum, home to Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch' and Vermeer's masterpieces. Book tickets online in advance to save time and potentially access discounts (~€22.50 adult).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes to the Van Gogh Museum Experience for an immersive afternoon among the world's largest collection of Van Gogh's works, including over 200 paintings. Pre-book tickets online (~€22 adult). Afterward, relax in the adjacent Vondelpark — Amsterdam's beloved green lung — which is completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward the canal ring. Walk along the famous '9 Straatjes' (Nine Streets) shopping district for window browsing. End the evening with a canal-side drink at a brown café (bruine kroeg) — a quintessentially Dutch experience.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh bread, cheese, and fruit from the Albert Heijn supermarket near the hotel for a self-made budget breakfast (~€3-5).
meals.lunch: Eat at Museumplein — pack a lunch from the supermarket or grab a falafel wrap from a nearby street vendor (~€5-8).
meals.dinner: Try Moeders restaurant for hearty Dutch home cooking at reasonable prices (~€15-18 per person), or opt for a FEBO automat for a true Dutch fast-food experience (~€5-8).

day_by_day.notes: Book Rijksmuseum and Van Gogh Museum tickets online at least 2-3 days in advance — both museums frequently sell out, especially in May. Combine both museums in one day since they are a 10-minute walk apart, maximizing your travel efficiency.

day_by_day.morning: Start with the Anne Frank House Tour — one of Amsterdam's most profound experiences. Walk through the hidden annex where Anne Frank and her family hid during World War II. Tickets must be booked months in advance online (~€16 adult). Arrive at your timed entry slot and allow 1.5-2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Canal Ring Boat Tour — a guided glass-topped boat cruise through Amsterdam's UNESCO-listed 17th-century canal ring (~€15-18 per person). Depart from near the Anne Frank House or Centraal Station. This offers a completely different perspective of the city and covers much of the historic ring in about 1 hour.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant De Pijp neighborhood for dinner and evening atmosphere. Visit the Albert Cuyp Market (open until 17:00 on weekdays) for cheap snacks and local produce if timing allows. De Pijp is known for its multicultural food scene and lively café culture.

meals.breakfast: Visit Bakkerij St. Dalfons or a local bakery near the hotel for fresh pastries and coffee (~€4-6).
meals.lunch: Grab a quick lunch near the Anne Frank House — try Café 't Smalle or pick up a herring (haring) from a street fish stall, a classic Amsterdam snack (~€4-7).
meals.dinner: Dine in De Pijp at Warung Spang-Makandra (Surinamese-Javanese cuisine, very affordable and authentic) for ~€10-13, or try one of the many international restaurants on Ferdinand Bolstraat.

day_by_day.notes: The Anne Frank House is the most important booking to secure before your trip — tickets often sell out weeks or months in advance. The canal boat tour is best enjoyed on a clear day; May weather in Amsterdam can be variable so bring a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Amsterdam's free and low-cost cultural gems. Visit the Amsterdam Museum (Amsterdams Historisch Museum) or the free Begijnhof — a hidden medieval courtyard dating to the 14th century, one of Amsterdam's best-kept secrets. Then walk through the Spui square, a hub for booksellers and intellectuals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to NEMO Science Museum or the Eastern Docklands (Java-eiland and KNSM-eiland) for a free architectural walking tour of Amsterdam's modern urban development. Alternatively, rent a bike (~€10-12/day) and cycle through the Plantage neighborhood, visiting the free exterior of Artis Zoo and the Hortus Botanicus garden (~€10 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the canal ring area for a sunset walk along the Amstel River. Visit the Magere Brug (Skinny Bridge) — Amsterdam's most famous drawbridge — beautifully lit in the evening. Enjoy a drink at a canal-side terrace.

meals.breakfast: Visit Noordermarkt (if it's a Saturday) for organic produce and Dutch pancakes, or grab a coffee and croissant from a local café (~€4-6).
meals.lunch: Try Broodje Bert or any local broodjeszaak (sandwich shop) for a classic Dutch lunch of uitsmijter (open-faced egg sandwich) for ~€6-9.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple dinner using groceries from Albert Heijn or Lidl to save money (~€5-8 per person), or dine at Café de Jaren for affordable Dutch café food with a great Amstel River view (~€12-16).

day_by_day.notes: Day 4 is intentionally lighter on paid attractions to balance the budget after the museum-heavy days. The Begijnhof is completely free and should not be missed — enter through the inconspicuous door on Gedempte Begijnensloot. Bike rental is highly recommended as cycling is the most authentic Amsterdam experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Amsterdam — visit the Waterlooplein Flea Market (open Mon-Sat) for unique souvenirs and vintage finds at bargain prices. Browse the stalls along the Amstel riverbank and pick up affordable Dutch gifts like stroopwafels, Delft-style ceramics, or vintage prints.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a final leisurely walk through the Plantage and Jewish Quarter, visiting the free exterior of the Portuguese Synagogue and the Hollandsche Schouwburg memorial (free entry). End with a visit to Artis Royal Zoo gardens or simply sit by the Entrepotdok canal for a peaceful farewell to Amsterdam.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to collect luggage if departing, or enjoy a final canal-side dinner in the Jordaan. Reflect on the trip with a classic Dutch jenever (gin) at a traditional proeflokaal (tasting house) like Wynand Fockink near Centraal Station.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a proper Dutch breakfast at Café Bern or Greenwoods (~€8-12) as a final morning indulgence.
meals.lunch: Grab poffertjes (mini Dutch pancakes) or a kroketten (croquette) from a street stall near Waterlooplein for an authentic and cheap lunch (~€4-7).
meals.dinner: Final dinner at De Vliegende Schotel (vegetarian, very affordable and popular with locals) for ~€12-15, or splurge slightly at a traditional Dutch restaurant for stamppot or erwtensoep (pea soup) to end the trip on a cultural note (~€15-20).

day_by_day.notes: If departing by flight, allow at least 2.5-3 hours before departure for the train journey to Schiphol (€5, 17 mins from Centraal) plus airport security. Amsterdam Centraal to Schiphol trains run every 10-15 minutes. Keep your OV-chipkaart topped up for the airport journey. Total estimated budget for 5 days excluding flights and accommodation: €150-200 per person covering museum entries, transport, and meals.

trip_options.title: Classic Amsterdam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Rijksmuseum Visit
experiences.description: Explore the Netherlands' premier art and history museum, home to masterpieces by Rembrandt, Vermeer, and other Dutch Golden Age painters. The collection spans 800 years of Dutch art and history across 80 galleries.

experiences.description: Walk through the hidden annex where Anne Frank and her family hid during World War II. A deeply moving and historically significant cultural experience that offers profound insight into wartime Amsterdam and Jewish heritage.

experiences.name: Jordaan Neighborhood Food & Culture Walk
experiences.description: Wander through Amsterdam's most charming historic neighborhood, stopping at the famous Noordermarkt for local cheeses, stroopwafels, and herring. Visit independent galleries, boutique shops, and hidden courtyards (hofjes) that reveal authentic Dutch daily life.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight KL arrives at 13:00. Travel from Amsterdam Airport Schiphol to Canal House Amsterdam (~30–45 min by train or taxi). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely stroll along the Herengracht and Prinsengracht canals near the hotel to get your bearings. Explore the immediate Grachtengordel (Canal Ring) neighborhood on foot — admire the iconic 17th-century canal houses, bridges, and houseboats at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Leidseplein or Spui square area for a relaxed first evening. Explore a few side streets and wind down after travel.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at Schiphol Airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite near Centraal Station or on arrival — try Broodje Bert or a stroopwafel and coffee from a street stall (€5–10)
meals.dinner: Café de Jaren on the Amstel — a beloved Amsterdam grand café with Dutch and international dishes, canal views, and a relaxed atmosphere. Mains €16–24.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light given travel fatigue. Pick up an OV-chipkaart (public transport card) at Schiphol or Centraal Station for easy tram and metro access throughout the trip. The hotel's canal house location puts you steps from most attractions.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit — Spend a rich morning at the Netherlands' premier art and history museum. Arrive at opening (9:00) to beat crowds. Marvel at Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch,' Vermeer's 'The Milkmaid,' and Delftware collections. Allow 2.5–3 hours. Book tickets online in advance (€22.50).
day_by_day.afternoon: Van Gogh Museum Experience — Just a 5-minute walk from the Rijksmuseum, dive into the world's largest collection of Van Gogh's works. Over 200 paintings including 'The Bedroom' and 'Almond Blossom.' Pre-book timed entry tickets (€22). Afterward, relax in the Museumplein park if weather permits.
day_by_day.evening: Walk or tram to the De Pijp neighborhood — Amsterdam's vibrant bohemian quarter. Browse the Albert Cuyp Market stalls (closes ~17:30) for snacks and souvenirs, then enjoy the lively neighborhood atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or nearby — try Lot Sixty One Coffee Roasters in Jordaan for excellent coffee and pastries (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Museumplein area — Café Cobra in Museumplein offers Dutch sandwiches and soups with terrace seating (€12–18)
meals.dinner: Brasserie Harkema in De Pijp or nearby — a stylish but relaxed brasserie with French-Dutch cuisine. Mains €18–26. Alternatively, try Surinamese-Dutch fusion at Roopram Roti for a budget-friendly local favorite (€10–15).

day_by_day.notes: This is the heaviest museum day — pace yourself with breaks. Both museums are within easy walking distance of each other and about 20 minutes' walk or a short tram ride from Canal House Amsterdam. Museum tickets MUST be pre-booked online to guarantee entry.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour — One of Amsterdam's most profound and important experiences. Walk through the hidden annex where Anne Frank and her family hid during WWII. Deeply moving and historically significant. Tickets must be booked weeks in advance online (€16). Located in the Jordaan, a short walk from the hotel. Allow 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jordaan Neighborhood Food & Culture Walk — Transition naturally from the Anne Frank House into exploring the charming Jordaan district. Visit the Noordermarkt area, browse independent galleries, boutique shops, and hidden hofjes (courtyard gardens). Stop at the Westerkerk tower for panoramic views of the canal ring (€9 to climb). Soak in the authentic Amsterdam neighborhood atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in the Jordaan for dinner, then enjoy an evening canal walk — the canals are beautifully lit after dark. Consider a post-dinner drink at a traditional Dutch 'brown café' (bruine kroeg).

meals.breakfast: Winkel 43 on Noordermarkt — famous for its apple pie and coffee, a true Amsterdam institution (€8–12). Perfect pre-Anne Frank House stop.
meals.lunch: Grab street food or a light bite during the Jordaan walk — try a herring sandwich (broodje haring) from a street cart (€4–6) or a lunch stop at Café 't Smalle, a historic Jordaan brown café (€10–15)
meals.dinner: Toscanini in the Jordaan — a beloved Italian restaurant with an open kitchen and warm atmosphere, popular with locals. Mains €18–28. Book ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Anne Frank House tickets are extremely limited — book as far in advance as possible (often 2+ months). Morning slots tend to be less crowded. The entire day is walkable from the hotel, making this a wonderfully immersive neighborhood day.

day_by_day.morning: Canal Ring Boat Tour — Cruise through Amsterdam's UNESCO-listed 17th-century canal ring aboard a guided glass-topped boat. Depart from the Damrak or Singelgracht area. See the city from the water — the Golden Bend, the Amstel River, and historic warehouses. Tours typically run 1–1.5 hours (€18–25). Book ahead or arrive early for popular morning departures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Amsterdam's historic center on foot. Visit the Dam Square and the Royal Palace (Koninklijk Paleis) exterior and interior (€12.50), then wander through the atmospheric Begijnhof — a hidden medieval courtyard and one of Amsterdam's best-kept secrets, free to enter. Browse the Spui square area and nearby bookshops.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Rembrandtplein area for a lively evening. This central square is surrounded by bars, restaurants, and street performers. Enjoy the energy of the city's nightlife district at a comfortable, relaxed pace.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or try Bakers & Roasters near De Pijp — a popular brunch spot with New Zealand-inspired dishes (€12–18). Slightly further but worth it.
meals.lunch: Central Amsterdam — Dampkring Coffee Shop area or try Gartine, a charming hidden tearoom near the Spui with homemade sandwiches and soups using market-fresh ingredients (€12–16). Small and intimate — arrive early.
meals.dinner: Rijsel on Marcusstraat — a beloved Amsterdam bistro serving Flemish-French rotisserie chicken and seasonal dishes in a converted school gymnasium. Excellent value and quality. Mains €18–24. Reservations recommended.

day_by_day.notes: The boat tour gives a completely different perspective of Amsterdam and is a highlight for canal lovers. If weather is poor, the glass-topped boats still operate comfortably. The afternoon walk is entirely flat and central, connecting all key historic landmarks.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a slow final morning in Amsterdam. Take a peaceful walk along the Amstel River or revisit a favorite canal street. Browse the local flower market (Bloemenmarkt on the Singel) for Dutch tulip bulbs or gifts — open from 9:00 (€3–15 for bulbs/souvenirs). Visit a local cheese shop such as Henri Willig for tastings and to pick up Dutch Gouda or Edam to take home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time — check out of Canal House Amsterdam (standard checkout 11:00–12:00, arrange luggage storage if needed). Final coffee and stroopwafel at a canal-side café. Head to Amsterdam Centraal Station for the Schiphol Airport train (16 min, €5.40) with ample time before your flight.

meals.breakfast: Final Amsterdam breakfast — Dignita Hoftuin near the Amstel, a social enterprise café with beautiful garden seating and excellent eggs, granola, and coffee (€10–16)
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch near Centraal Station or Schiphol — try Stach Food for high-quality Dutch open-faced sandwiches and salads (€10–14)
meals.dinner: At Schiphol Airport or on the flight

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the train journey to Schiphol (16 min) plus airport security and boarding. Store luggage at the hotel or at Centraal Station lockers (€6–9) to keep your final morning hands-free and enjoyable. The Bloemenmarkt is a lovely, low-key final activity that captures the essence of Amsterdam.

trip_options.title: Premium Amsterdam Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.description: Wander through Amsterdam's most charming historic neighborhood, stopping at the famous Noordermarkt for local cheeses, stroopwafels, and herring. Visit independent galleries, boutique shops, and hidden courtyards (hofjes) that reveal authentic Dutch daily life.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Hotel Check-In: Flight KL lands at 13:00, so morning is reserved for travel. Take a private airport transfer from Schiphol to Canal House Amsterdam. Settle into your luxury canal-view suite, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome amenity from the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Canal Ring Boat Tour: Step directly into Amsterdam's iconic waterways with a guided glass-topped private boat tour through the UNESCO-listed 17th-century canal ring. Departing from a nearby jetty, your expert guide will narrate the history of the Golden Age merchant houses, hidden churches, and iconic bridges as you glide through Prinsengracht, Herengracht, and Keizersgracht.
day_by_day.evening: Jordaan Neighborhood Stroll & Dinner: Take a leisurely evening walk through the charming Jordaan district, just steps from the hotel. Browse boutique galleries and admire gaslit canal reflections before dinner at Restaurant Breda (Singel 210), a celebrated fine-dining destination known for its creative Dutch-French tasting menus and outstanding wine cellar.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the plane or a light welcome spread arranged by Canal House Amsterdam upon check-in.
meals.lunch: Light bite at Café Papeneiland (Prinsengracht 2), a historic 17th-century brown café serving classic Dutch apple pie and open-faced sandwiches — a perfect first taste of Amsterdam.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Breda (Singel 210) — award-winning tasting menu featuring seasonal Dutch ingredients, artisan cheeses, and a curated wine pairing in an intimate, candlelit setting.

day_by_day.notes: Request a canal-facing room at check-in for the best views. Pre-book the private boat tour in advance as premium slots fill quickly in May. Confirm your dinner reservation at Breda at least 2–3 weeks ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit: Begin your morning with a private guided tour of the Netherlands' premier art and history museum. Marvel at Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch,' Vermeer's 'The Milkmaid,' and a vast collection of Delftware and Golden Age artifacts. A private guide ensures you bypass queues and gain exclusive insight into the masterpieces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Van Gogh Museum Experience: A short walk from the Rijksmuseum, immerse yourself in the world's largest collection of Van Gogh's works — over 200 paintings including 'Sunflowers' and 'Almond Blossom.' Opt for a curator-led private session for an in-depth exploration of Van Gogh's life, technique, and emotional journey through his art.
day_by_day.evening: Cocktails & Fine Dining in the Museum Quarter: Begin the evening with craft cocktails at Bar Americain inside the iconic Americain Hotel (Leidsekade 97), a stunning Art Deco landmark. Follow with dinner at Brasserie van Baerle (Van Baerlestraat 158), a beloved Amsterdam institution serving refined French-Dutch cuisine with impeccable service.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam — expect freshly baked pastries, smoked salmon, artisan cheeses, and specialty coffee in the elegant dining room overlooking the canal.
meals.lunch: Rijksmuseum's exclusive Michelin-recommended restaurant, Rijks — enjoy a beautifully presented Dutch lunch menu with seasonal produce in the museum's stunning atrium.
meals.dinner: Brasserie van Baerle — classic French-Dutch cuisine with an extensive wine list; known for its elegant ambiance and loyal local following among Amsterdam's cultural elite.

day_by_day.notes: Book timed-entry tickets for both the Rijksmuseum and Van Gogh Museum well in advance — May is peak season. Private guided tours can be arranged through the hotel concierge. Allow at least 2 hours per museum.

day_by_day.morning: Jordaan Neighborhood Food & Culture Walk: Join a premium small-group or private food and culture walk through Amsterdam's most beloved historic neighborhood. Stop at the famous Noordermarkt Sunday organic market, sample Dutch stroopwafels, artisan cheeses, and fresh herring, and explore hidden courtyards (hofjes) and independent art galleries that define the Jordaan's bohemian spirit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Anne Frank House Tour: Experience one of Europe's most profoundly moving cultural sites. Walk through the hidden annex where Anne Frank and her family sheltered during World War II. A private or priority-access guided tour adds historical context and ensures a respectful, unhurried visit. Afterward, take time to reflect with a quiet walk along Prinsengracht.
day_by_day.evening: Herengracht Canal Dinner Cruise: Elevate your evening with a premium private dinner cruise along the Herengracht — Amsterdam's most prestigious canal, known as the 'Golden Bend.' Enjoy a chef-prepared multi-course Dutch menu, fine wines, and champagne as the city's illuminated bridges and 17th-century mansions glide past.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam, followed by early market tastings during the Jordaan walk.
meals.lunch: Café de Reiger (Nieuwe Leliestraat 34) in the Jordaan — a beloved neighborhood bistro with a seasonal menu, natural wines, and a warm, convivial atmosphere beloved by locals.
meals.dinner: Private luxury dinner cruise on the Herengracht canals — a bespoke catered experience arranged through the hotel concierge, featuring a 4-course Dutch-French menu with wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Anne Frank House tickets must be booked months in advance — this is non-negotiable in peak season. The Sunday Noordermarkt runs from 09:00–16:00, so time the walk accordingly. The evening dinner cruise should be reserved at least 4–6 weeks ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Stedelijk Museum & Contemporary Art Scene: Explore Amsterdam's world-class museum of modern and contemporary art and design, the Stedelijk Museum, adjacent to the Rijksmuseum. Discover works by Mondrian, Malevich, Warhol, and Appel alongside cutting-edge contemporary installations. Consider a private docent tour for deeper engagement with the collection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury Shopping & Antique Galleries on Spiegelstraat: Spend the afternoon browsing the prestigious Spiegelkwartier antiques district, home to over 80 specialist dealers selling Dutch Golden Age paintings, Delftware, vintage maps, and decorative arts. Continue to the P.C. Hooftstraat — Amsterdam's equivalent of Bond Street — for luxury fashion boutiques including Hermès, Chanel, and Dries Van Noten.
day_by_day.evening: Cocktail Experience & Michelin-Starred Dinner: Begin the evening at Tales & Spirits (Lijnbaanssteeg 5–7), one of Amsterdam's most acclaimed craft cocktail bars, known for its theatrical, ingredient-forward drinks program. Conclude with dinner at Ciel Bleu (Hotel Okura, Ferdinand Bolstraat 333) — a two-Michelin-starred restaurant on the 23rd floor offering breathtaking city panoramas and an extraordinary contemporary French tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam — take your time with fresh-pressed juices, Dutch cheeses, and warm pastries before a mid-morning museum start.
meals.lunch: Librije's Zusje Amsterdam (Waldorf Astoria, Herengracht 542–556) — the hotel's acclaimed restaurant offering a refined Dutch lunch in one of Amsterdam's most beautiful historic canal house settings.
meals.dinner: Ciel Bleu at Hotel Okura — two Michelin stars, panoramic Amsterdam skyline views, and a world-class wine cellar. Reserve the chef's tasting menu with full wine pairing for the ultimate experience.

day_by_day.notes: Ciel Bleu reservations are essential and should be made 4–6 weeks in advance. Request a window table when booking for the best city views. The Spiegelkwartier galleries are generally open Monday afternoons but confirm hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private Canal Kayak or Stand-Up Paddleboard Experience: For a final morning on the water, enjoy a private guided kayak or SUP session through Amsterdam's quieter inner canals — a unique, intimate perspective unavailable on larger boats. Glide past historic houseboats, hidden gardens, and centuries-old warehouses as the city wakes up around you.
day_by_day.afternoon: Royal Palace Amsterdam & Dam Square: Visit the magnificent Royal Palace on Dam Square, originally built as Amsterdam's City Hall in 1655 and still used by the Dutch Royal Family for official functions. Explore its opulent interiors, marble floors, and priceless artworks. Afterward, visit the nearby Nieuwe Kerk for its rotating exhibitions of international cultural significance.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Champagne & Gala Dinner: Return to the hotel for a final champagne toast on your canal-view terrace or in the elegant lounge. For your farewell dinner, dine at De Kas (Kamerlingh Onneslaan 3) — a legendary Amsterdam restaurant set inside a 1926 greenhouse, serving a hyper-seasonal tasting menu where nearly every ingredient is grown on-site or sourced within 50 km. A truly unforgettable final evening.

meals.breakfast: A special final breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam — request an outdoor table by the canal if weather permits, with a full spread of Dutch specialties, fresh fruit, and champagne to celebrate the journey.
meals.lunch: Café Hoppe (Spui 18–20) — one of Amsterdam's oldest and most atmospheric brown cafés, dating to 1670. Enjoy a classic Dutch lunch of bitterballen, aged Gouda, and a crisp Dutch lager in historic surroundings.
meals.dinner: De Kas — a greenhouse dining experience unlike any other in Amsterdam. The single tasting menu changes daily based on what was harvested that morning. Pair with their exceptional biodynamic wine selection for a sublime farewell meal.

day_by_day.notes: The morning kayak session is best booked for 08:00–09:00 to enjoy calm canals before tourist boat traffic increases. Confirm checkout arrangements with Canal House Amsterdam the evening before. De Kas is located slightly outside the center — arrange a private car transfer through the hotel concierge.
